title: Moody Storm-Beam Landscape: Zone-Based Processing, Sky Extension, and Beams Emphasis in Photoshop

date.basis: embedded_creation_time metadata; transcript does not independently confirm the shoot date

summary: This video presents a field-to-processor workflow for building a moody, multi-shot storm landscape. Starting with scene assessment and layering cues (fog boundaries and atmospheric beams), the presenter selects shots with strong layer separation, then builds a composite by expanding sky, integrating beams, and preserving shadow detail through non-destructive editing. The workflow emphasizes zone-based processing (mountains/clouds in shadow, beams, and sky), sky extension via cloning and edge blending, and careful color and tonal grading to keep a cohesive moody palette. Throughout, the instructor highlights non-destructive history states, framing/compositional decisions (including the rule of trapezoids to create a wider feel), and practical notes about workflow order, alternative widening methods, and optional tools like Topaz for refinement.

sections.title: Scene evaluation and composition planning
sections.description: Initial assessment of the landscape notes multiple atmospheric layers (ridge/fog interactions) and discusses maintaining distinction between layers to enable strong compositions; mentions being positioned at the right distance to emphasize layer separation.

sections.title: Beam discovery and shadow detail extraction
sections.description: Explores candidate frames with visible beams and distinct atmospheric layers; emphasizes avoiding overexposure in highlights and preserving shadow detail, noting the importance of capturing or preserving beam geometry for later processing.

sections.title: Best-beam selection and separation assessment
sections.description: Continues evaluation of frames, identifying which shot provides the clearest layer separation and beam placement; selects a candidate where the left-right angle enhances the beams while keeping layer distinction intact.

sections.title: Sky extension and sky-beam integration workflow
sections.description: Describes merging multiple skies and beams: expanding the sky to accommodate beams, aligning sky elements, and using soft brushes and clone stamping to blend sources; mentions the use of a third image to supply upper-right sky and discusses edge fading for seamless integration.

sections.title: Non-destructive editing workflow and edge refinement
sections.description: Introduces non-destructive workflow via history states, describing how history steps can be blended and refined like layers; demonstrates refining hard-edged separations and adjusting edges to preserve natural transitions between elements.

sections.title: Rule-based composition widening and irreversibility caution
sections.description: Outlines compositional widening to mimic a wider lens (top/bottom pressure) and cautions that changes after applying these steps are irreversible beyond the saved history state; mentions distort/scale in RAW and wide-angle adaptive filter as alternative widening methods.

sections.title: Zone-based processing framework
sections.description: Defines a zone processing approach: identify regions requiring separate, independent adjustments (especially beams and shadowed areas) and apply targeted tonal/color edits per zone before blending for a cohesive result.

sections.title: Beam isolation with Auto HDR and luminosity sculpting
sections.description: Demonstrates isolating and intensifying beams using Auto HDR-like parameter presets, then enhancing them with luminosity-based adjustments and localized color grading to maintain mood without blowing out highlights.

sections.title: Final touches, mood tuning, and workflow philosophy
sections.description: Covers final mood adjustments (dark, moody, slightly cooler), optional use of Topaz for noise/detail, minor beam refinements, and a reminder that technical adjustments precede artistic color/light work; ends with intent to save/export.
